questions.question:
**In the sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

I learnt to adapt myself quickly to new schools because we moved to new places quite frequent.

options.text: I learnt to adapt myself quickly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**quite frequent'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the usage of the adjective** 'frequent'.**
 
• The phrase** 'quite frequent'** is modifying the verb** 'moved'**. This is incorrect.
 
• For the sentence to be correct, we need to use the adverbial phrase** 'quite frequently' **to modify the verb** 'moved'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Frequent is an adjective. It means occurring or done many times at short intervals.
 
• 'Frequently' is an adverb. It means often. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Adjectives do not modify verbs or adverbs or other adjectives.
 
• But adjectives can also act as a complement to linking verbs or the verb to be.
 
 
• It smells** disgusting **when you take off your shoes. (The adjective 'disgusting' complements the verb 'smells'.)

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Roopa said to me, "Please accompany me to the market."

options.text: Roopa said please accompany me to the market.
Roopa said to me that you must accompany me to the market.
Roopa is requesting me to accompany her to the market.
Roopa requested me to accompany her to the market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Roopa requested me to accompany her to the market.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given direct speech is an imperative sentence. An imperative sentence is a sentence that expresses a command, a request, advice, or a suggestion.
 
 
• *Open the door. **(Command)***
 
• *Please help me.** (Request)***
 
• *Quit smoking.** (Advice.)***
 
 
 
• As imperative sentences have a command, a request, advice, or a suggestion, to change them into an indirect speech some specific verbs are used (requested, order, advised, forbade, suggested) to replace the verbs (e.g. told, said) of reporting verb.
 
• In the given sentence, 'please' is used which gives the tone of requesting somebody. Hence, use *'requested' in the reported speech.*

**So the correct Indirect speech is**→* Roopa **requested **me to accompany her to the market.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Some such common events that bring us happiness for a short time include passing an exam, getting a job, going on a vacation or buying a dream house.

B. Happiness is more difficult to achieve than peace as we keep striving for it daily.

C. Peace, on the other hand, is sustainable for many years, costs less energy, and doesn't depend on external events such as these.

D. Events that we struggle for in our daily lives to bring us happiness only come randomly, stay for a short time and subside.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BDAC'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The passage should start with** sentence B **that establishes the subject matter which is a comparison between happiness and peace. It states that happiness is difficult to achieve in comparison to peace. It mentions the reason behind this difficulty to be our constant need for happiness in daily life.
 
• To maintain continuity, **sentence D ** should come in next as it talks about how the events in our daily lives that provide happiness are random and occur for a short period. The context of daily life makes sentence D ideal for the **second position**.
 
• **Sentence A **should come in the **third spot** as it further elaborates on the instances mentioned in **sentence D** that brings us happiness. It mentions several examples of instances that provide us with happiness.
 
• **Sentence C **provides an example of peace and points out how it differs from happiness. It comes in the last spot. 
 
• So, **BDAC ** is the correct arrangement of sentences which makes **option 4 **the correct answer.

We are arranging an exhibition of sarees from different states of India at Dilli Haat.

An exhibition of sarees from different states of India is being arranged by us at Dilli Haat.

• *The given sentence is in the active voice which we can see because the passive voice is always written in the form of 'Be + V₃'*
 
• While changing the subject in the active voice, change it into the object of the passive voice.
 
• Always remember that the tense never changes in the Active/Passive voice.
 
• In the given sentence, the tense is the present continuous tense. So, the structure in the passive voice is **'Subject + Be + Being + V₃ + Object'**
 
• The verb 'Arrange' is a transitive verb so the direct object is 'an exhibition' which is going to be the subject in the passive voice.
 
• Also, it is a singular noun so we have used the singular verb.

**So the correct passive voice is**→ ***An exhibition** of sarees from different states of India** is being** arranged by us at Dilli Haat.*

questions.question: Salma buys an article and then sells if for Rs. 810. If she loses 10%, then at what price should she sell it to gain 4%?

**Given:**

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (1 + P%/100)

SP = CP × (1 – L%/100)

where, SP → Selling Price, CP → Cost Price

**Calculations:**

At loss 10%, SP of article = Rs. 810

Now, SP = CP × (1 – L%/100)

⇒ 810 = CP × (1 – 10/100)

⇒ 810 = CP × (9/10) ----(1)

At gain 4%, 

SP = CP × (1 + 4/100)

⇒ SP = CP × (26/25) ----(2)

Dividing (2) by (1), we get

⇒ SP/810 = [CP × (26/25)]/[CP × (9/10)]

⇒ SP/810 = 104/9

⇒ SP = (104/90) × 810

⇒ SP = Rs. 936

**∴ The price at which Salma sells it to gain 4% is Rs. 936.**

questions.question: The process that moves, elevates or builds up portions of the earth’s crust is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**diastrophism**__.

__
 
• All processes that **move, elevate or build up portions of the earth’s crust** come under diastrophism.
 
• It includes Orogenic processes and Epeirogenic processes.
 
 
• **Orogenic processes** involving mountain building through severe folding and affecting long and narrow belts of the earth’s crust. They act tangentially to the earth's surface, as in plate tectonics.
 
• **Epeirogenic processes** involving uplift or warping of large parts of the earth’s crust, thus it is a continental building process. They act along the earth’s radius and thus are also called radial movements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 denudation
 
 
 
• All the exogenic geomorphic processes are covered in the denudation phenomenon.
 
• Weathering, mass wasting/movements, erosion, and transportation are included in denudation.
 
 
 
 

 volcanism
 
 
 
• It is the process where deep magma erupts onto the surface or emplaces near the surface through a volcanic conduit, thereby forming various types of volcanic debris.
 
 
 
 

 weathering
 
 
 
• It is a long term process of breaking down or dissolving of rocks and minerals on Earth's surface.
 
• Once a rock has been broken down, a process called erosion transports the bits of rock and minerals away.
 
• Water, acids, salt, plants, animals, and temperature changes are all agents of weathering and erosion.

questions.question: Slate is a which type of rock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**metamorphic**__.

__
 
• **Slate** is a fine-grained** metamorphic rock** that exhibits a foliation called **slaty cleavage** that is the flat orientation of the small platy crystals of mica and chlorite forming perpendicular to the direction of stress.
 
• Metamorphic rock material has been changed by **temperature, pressure, and/or fluids**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 sedimentary
 
 
 
• Sedimentary rocks are formed by the accumulation of sediments.
 
• There are three basic types of sedimentary rocks:
 
 
• Clastic sedimentary rocks such as breccia, conglomerate, sandstone, siltstone, and shale are formed from mechanical weathering debris.
 
• Chemical sedimentary rocks, such as rock salt, iron ore, chert, flint, some dolomites, and some limestones, form when dissolved materials precipitate from the solution.
 
• Organic sedimentary rocks such as chalk, coal, diatomite, some dolomites, and some limestones, form from the accumulation of plant or animal debris.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 volcanic
 
 
 
• Volcanic rock (extrusive rock) is one kind of magmatic rock (igneous rock).
 
• Once the lava has erupted, it cools and solidifies into rock.
 
• Basalt is a common volcanic rock with low silica content. Rhyolite is a volcanic rock with high silica content.
 
 
 
 

 igneous
 
 
 
• It forms when hot, molten rock crystallizes and solidifies. The melt originates deep within the Earth near active plate boundaries or hot spots, then rises toward the surface.
 
• Examples of intrusive igneous rocks are diabase, diorite, gabbro, granite, pegmatite, and peridotite.
